answer.question: How close should turf go to a Fleming Island pond or shoreline?
answer.answer: Where Florida’s residential turf standard applies, it generally requires a 10-foot waterbody setback, with an exception where a seawall or bulkhead separates the site. It also keeps turf out of swales, ditches and pond littoral areas. Confirm the boundary and applicable conditions before finalizing the layout.

blocks.h2: Choose the shots and leave room around them.
paras: A green can offer short-game practice without taking over the entire yard. Discuss cup positions, contours and any fringe after deciding the putting lines you want. Keep paths, planting and a separate pet area in the plan.
On a pine-shaded lot, include needle cleanup and tree-root constraints before choosing the turf boundary.

blocks.h2: Keep the drainage area doing its job.
paras: Mark the pond boundary, swales, drains and any maintenance access on the property plan. The existing stormwater system and required shoreline separation need to remain part of the layout, even if the fence extends farther.

Fleming Island Plantation, Eagle Harbor and Pace Island have different governing bodies and requirements. Obtain the current instructions for your property, including any architectural review and CDD conditions. Bring those responses to the estimate rather than relying on another community’s approval.
